name: slash-command-hardening

escalations.question: Backlog row 48 asks main to drop slash-command names that are not one printable token. Which names count as one printable token?
escalations.answer: At Gate 1: a name passes when it is non-empty and contains no whitespace (Unicode \s), no control character (\p{Cc}) and no format character (\p{Cf}). Unicode letters and plugin-qualified names such as sir:sir-up pass.

escalations.question: Gate 3 advisory (slash-commands.ts:64): stripping every \p{Cc} from description and argumentHint deletes tab, newline and CR, so words run together. Fixing it means amending C4. Fix now, carry to backlog, or drop?
escalations.answer: At Gate 3: fix now. C4 amended (A1) so whitespace control runs become one space; one fix round and a re-review, then approval is asked again over the final diff.

amendments.before: C4: `description` and `argumentHint` have every control character (\p{Cc}) and format character (\p{Cf}) removed, and an alias that fails C3's name rule is dropped while valid aliases keep their order; the module's docblock states these rules.
amendments.after: C4: In `description` and `argumentHint`, each run of one or more control characters that JavaScript's \s matches (tab, newline, vertical tab, form feed, CR) becomes a single space, and every other control character (\p{Cc}) and format character (\p{Cf}) is removed, so `a\tb` and `a\r\nb` both become `a b`; an alias that fails C3's name rule is dropped while valid aliases keep their order; the module's docblock states these rules.

criteria: C1: `#publishCommands` in src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts returns without calling `this.#push.podCommands` when `session.disposed` is true, so no `push:podCommands` is sent for a disposed session even when a caller forgets its own guard; its docblock says the check is at the choke point (the callers' own guards may stay).

C2: A unit test fails when the `session.disposed` check in `#publishCommands` is removed while a caller's guard is bypassed (shown by a red step or an injected defect), and every existing test in tests/unit/pod-manager/slash-commands-push.test.ts still passes, the disposed-session test included.

C3: `normalizeSlashCommands` in src/main/pod-manager/slash-commands.ts drops an entry whose `name` is empty or contains whitespace (Unicode \s), a control character (\p{Cc}) or a format character (\p{Cf}); names such as `sir:sir-up`, `mcp__srv__tool` and a non-ASCII letter name are kept, in order.

C4: In `description` and `argumentHint`, each run of one or more control characters that JavaScript's \s matches (tab, newline, vertical tab, form feed, CR) becomes a single space, and every other control character (\p{Cc}) and format character (\p{Cf}) is removed, so `a\tb` and `a\r\nb` both become `a b`; an alias that fails C3's name rule is dropped while valid aliases keep their order; the module's docblock states these rules.

C5: Unit tests cover C3 and C4 with must-drop cases (a space, a tab, a newline, a NUL, a zero-width or bidi format character) and must-keep near-misses (`sir:sir-up`, `mcp__srv__tool`, a non-ASCII name, a description with an ordinary space).

C6: `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass from the repository root, and no file is changed outside the two source files and their unit tests (tests/unit/pod-manager/slash-commands.test.ts, tests/unit/pod-manager/slash-commands-push.test.ts).
